newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AEGON TARGETS FURTHER PHILIPPINE GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: AEGON TARGETS FURTHER PHILIPPINE GROWTH.

text.p: Dutch Aegon NV said it was on the lookout for partners in the Philippines since after this week winning a licence to start life insurance business in this emerging market.

"We are on the lookout for partners in the Philippines and do not rule out an acquisition, although it would only be a small takeover as possibilities for a takeover are not great in this region," said Aegon chairman Kees Storm in a telephone interview from the United States, where he is currently meeting analysts and bourse officials.

Earlier this week Aegon and ING Insurance, an arm of financial services giant ING Group, won licences to start life insurance businesses in the Philippines, arising from an official visit to the country by Dutch prime minister Wim Kok.
Storm said Aegon could also opt for a start on its own in the Philippines, but then it would take longer to develop business, which is set to start by the end of 1997.
Aegon said on Thursday the market for life insurance in the Philippines generated a total premium income of about 750 million guilders in 1994.
"Premium income in this sector (in the Philippines) increases by about 20 percent annually," Storm said on Friday.
Aegon lies in wait to set up business in other Asian countries, but Storm said it had not currently applied for any other licences.
"Thailand is one of the countries that is top of the list for us though," said Storm, adding Aegon would not enter that market in 1996. "Not this year, but 1997 is possible", he said.
Aegon started its first Asian adventure at the end of 1993 when it opened an office in Taiwan.
The greenfield operation in Taiwan is not break-even yet, but Storm said this could be the case in 1998.
Aegon, which will publish third quarter results next week, posted first half profits of 711 million guilders.
Storm said Aegon had put aside two billion guilders for new acquisitions, but he would not specify any takeover targets.
